drafts.title: Lane-keeping and highway assistance steer smoothly without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: When highway assistance or lane-keeping assist is active, the car should provide smooth, predictable steering in curves and avoid abrupt corrective steering that surprises the driver or feels nervous.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In an independent 100-mile highway test (mixed straight and curved segments, speeds 50–80 mph), lane-keeping assist must complete ≥95% of driven distance without any 'abrupt steering correction' (defined as a steering-induced lateral deviation >0.5 m within 2 s). While active, the system's RMS lateral deviation must be ≤0.25 m.
assumptions: Highway routes used in tests reflect typical US highway geometry and traffic; maps and basic sensor data available for lane guidance.
Where regulatory approval is required for hands-off operation, the system may operate in driver-supervised lane-keeping mode until approvals are granted.
uncertainties: Performance degradation in severe weather, heavy crosswind, or when lane markings are degraded.
Driver acceptance thresholds for 'smooth' steering vary; the acceptance criterion uses an objective threshold derived from driver studies.

drafts.title: Charge port indicator and trip planner make charging state and compatible fast chargers obvious
drafts.description: Drivers must be able to see the charge/charging status at a glance at the charge port, and the route planner must reliably find and clearly mark compatible fast chargers for long trips so locating a usable charger is fast and unambiguous.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: a) Charge-port indicator must present distinct, easily discriminable visual states (charging, complete, error, ready-to-plug) readable from 1.5 m in daylight; 95% of users in a daylight readability test must correctly identify state. b) For a sample of 200 representative US intercity routes (each ≥50 miles), the vehicle route planner must identify at least one compatible DC fast charger on 95% of routes within 5 seconds and display connector type and estimated max power.
assumptions: Up-to-date charger network and connector-type data are available via partner networks or roaming agreements.
Driver-facing readability test uses standard daylight luminance levels (as defined in vehicle HMI test protocols).
uncertainties: Real-time charger availability and power capability can change quickly; planner accuracy depends on network data freshness.
Different charger networks may provide different metadata completeness (connector type, real-time power).

drafts.title: Offer a long-range powertrain variant delivering at least 600 miles real-world range
drafts.description: Provide at least one available powertrain configuration that gives drivers a real-world single-tank or single-charge range of 600 miles so long trips require fewer stops and reduce range anxiety.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one sold powertrain variant (ICE, hybrid, or equivalent) achieves ≥600 miles real-world range, measured on a US highway cycle at 70 mph and averaged across three representative intercity routes, validated by an independent third-party test.
assumptions: The long-range outcome can be met by an ICE or hybrid variant (not necessarily a pure battery-electric variant) within the successor timeframe.
Real-world test protocol and routes are agreed with the validation lab and reflect typical US highway driving.
uncertainties: Real-world range depends on optional equipment, payload, wheel/tire choice and driving style.
Fuel availability or EV charging infrastructure expectations may change customer perception of required range.

drafts.title: Reduce harsh ride on broken pavement and lower distracting wind noise at highway speeds
drafts.description: Improve ride compliance over broken pavement and reduce wind-related cabin noise so that long-distance driving and highway travel feel less fatiguing and less distracting.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: a) On a standardized broken-pavement route, a 10-person blinded occupant panel must report perceived ride harshness improved by ≥20% versus the current model (same test, same tires). b) Cabin wind noise measured at the driver's ear at 75 mph with a 10 mph crosswind must be ≤67 dB(A) (targeting at least a 3 dB reduction vs the current model).
assumptions: Current-model baseline data are available for direct comparison and tests use identical tire and load conditions.
Road and wind test conditions are reproducible and standardized (test track / wind-tunnel protocols).
uncertainties: Different wheel/tire options or optional aerodynamic packages will affect measured noise and comfort.
Perceived comfort is partially subjective; blending objective measures with panel scores reduces ambiguity.
